| [NOTE-090](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-090.md) v2 | LLMs are stochastic measuring devices | The chapter argues by analogy that deep neural networks are "stochastic measuring devices". Training alters the parameters in response to data, so that the resulting configuration carries information about the data ("training is measurement"). The trained weights are a model, and generation is simulation. DNNs are stochastic because random initialisation and non-convex loss mean runs need not converge to the same weights, failing Baird's "regularity" condition. The problems of interpreting model states and generated text are therefore the familiar problems of instruments, models and simulations. The problem of interpretable AI is an instance of the coordination problem in the philosophy of measurement. | Read |
| [NOTE-102](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-102.md) v2 | Bottou & Schölkopf — Borges and AI | A short essay, not an argument with evidence. It claims that a "perfect language model", defined as sampling each next word from a random occurrence of the current text in the infinite collection of all plausible texts, is a fiction machine governed by "narrative necessity", to which "neither truth nor intention" matters. On that view hallucinations "are just confabulations", chat-bot answers take the role the user's framing implies, and fine-tuning and RLHF are attempts to prune the garden "against its nature". It warns that power over what LLMs write becomes "power over what we think". | Read |
| [NOTE-157](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-157.md) v2 | Roberts — Talkative AI and the fiction of artificial minds | If a substantial class of mental states (interoceptive, affective, perceptual, and bodily-agentive states such as effort, trying and ownership) depends on an animate body, then today's disembodied chatbots lack them, and their many self-ascriptions of such states are "systematically untrue". Roberts argues that users can nonetheless engage chatbots through make-believe, as a new kind of fictional character that is interactive, co-constructed, self-involving and blended with the real world. He argues that this fictionalist stance escapes the epistemic norms that bind realist belief. | Read |
| [NOTE-158](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-158.md) v2 | Grindrod et al. — Distributional semantics & holism | The authors argue that distributional models answer the instability objection to meaning holism if meaning is read "differentially", as a word's relations to its nearest neighbours, and not as its position in the space. They illustrate this with two corpus-expansion demonstrations. In a ±10-word count model on Stein's The Making of Americans (about 522k tokens), adding Hemingway's "A Clean, Well-Lighted Place" (under 1,500 words) shifts every cosine value for "know" by at most about 0.0005 (e.g. 0.95231 → 0.95284 for "understand") and leaves its top-10 neighbours in the same order, while "glass" gets a new neighbourhood. A Word2vec CBOW model on 143M words of Wikipedia shows the same pattern when about 21M words of the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (SEP) are added: "atomism" shifts, "can" barely moves. The residual instability, they argue, is a virtue. | Read |
| [NOTE-179](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-179.md) | Brandom, inferentialism and meaning entitlement | Boghossian's objection to substantive, entitlement-based theories of meaning (drawn from pejoratives like "Boche") works against Dummett but not against Brandom. | [NOTE-245](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-245.md) | Mathematical Foundations for a Compositional Distributional Model of Meaning | The paper builds DisCoCat as a product category FVect × P of vector spaces and a free pregroup. A sentence's meaning is f(w₁⊗…⊗wₙ), where f is the linear map got by putting vector spaces in place of the pregroup types in the reduction p₁…pₙ ≤ s. The ε maps become inner products and the η maps become Σᵢ eᵢ⊗eᵢ. So "John likes Mary" is Σ_ijk c_ijk⟨v\|vᵢ⟩⟨w_k\|w⟩ sⱼ ∈ S, and "not" is the 2×2 swap matrix placed on the sentence wire. There is no theorem and no experiment. The sentence space S is shown only as 1- or 2-dimensional truth values, over a toy model with one basis vector per individual, and the paper says how neither S nor the verb tensors are to be built from data. Its headline similarity numbers (3/4, 1/4, 3/8) are unnormalised inner products. Under its own Definition 5.1 they are 0.949, 0.316 and 0.6. | Read |
| [NOTE-246](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-246.md) v2 | Reasoning about Meaning in Natural Language with Compact Closed Categories and Frobenius Algebras | The paper sets the sentence space equal to the noun space (F(s)=F(n)=W). It then uses the basis-copying map σ: v_i ↦ v_i⊗v_i of the Frobenius algebra fixed by W's basis to lift corpus-built verb matrices Σ_i sbj_i⊗obj_i into rank-3 tensors. So a transitive sentence becomes sbj⊙(verb·obj) ("copy-subject") or obj⊙(verbᵀ·sbj) ("copy-object"), a vector in W. On the Grefenstette–Sadrzadeh verb-disambiguation set, copy-object gets Spearman ρ=0.172, against 0.168 (Kron), 0.163 (Multp), 0.143 (copy-subject), 0.050 (additive) and an inter-annotator bound of 0.620. On a 112-term definition-matching task the best F1 is 0.21 (nouns) and 0.27 (verbs). No significance test is reported. The disambiguation numbers are identical to the authors' COLING 2012 paper, and the definition numbers are the same data re-reported. | Read |
| [NOTE-338](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-338.md) | Where Am I? | A first-person story with an argument inside. With his brain in a vat in Houston radio-linked to his body under Tulsa, the narrator tests three answers to "where am I?": where the body is, where the brain is, where the point of view is. He favours the third and finds it unclear. A computer duplicate of his brain can take over his body with no detectable difference, and when duplicate and brain drift out of step there are two persons in one body. Intuition pumps, no thesis defended to the end. | Read |
| [NOTE-349](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-349.md) | Searle — Minds, brains, and programs | A man who follows English rules for manipulating Chinese symbols can answer Chinese questions like a native speaker without understanding Chinese, so no program is by itself sufficient for understanding. Six replies are answered; the systems reply by having the man internalise the room. Searle grants that machines could think, if they had the brain's causal powers. The argument concerns intentionality, and its answer to the systems reply rests on treating the internalised system as a part of the man, which is the point in dispute. | Read |
| [NOTE-350](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-350.md) | Intentional Systems | Defines an Intentional system as anything whose behaviour can be predicted by ascribing beliefs and desires and assuming rationality, and makes the status relative to the predictor's strategy and indifferent to the system's matter and consciousness. Argues that Intentional theory is vacuous as psychology because it presupposes rationality, that behaviourism smuggles it in, and that every content-ascribing theory owes a "loan of intelligence" that must be repaid by analysing away a little man. Ends on belief's two norms, truth and accurate avowal. | Read |
| [NOTE-353](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-353.md) | True Believers: The Intentional Strategy and Why It Works | Belief is objective but visible only through a strategy: a true believer is any system "reliably and voluminously predictable" by treating it as a rational agent with the beliefs and desires it ought to have. Adopting the stance is free; its success is a fact, and Laplacean Martians who skipped it would miss real patterns. Thermostats and people differ in degree, by how tightly their states are tied to one interpretation. Evolution explains easily why the strategy works; how the machinery does it is open, and the language of thought is a bet, not a necessity. | Read |
| [NOTE-363](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-363.md) | Clark — Intrinsic content, active memory and the extended mind | Clark defends [LIT-097](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-097.md) against Adams and Aizawa's intrinsic-content objection: the notion is unclear, silicon could carry it, and their own concession that not every cognitive state needs non-derived content lets a conventional encoding serve as a belief's vehicle. | [NOTE-368](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-368.md) | Adams & Aizawa — The bounds of cognition | Adams and Aizawa grant [LIT-097](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-097.md)'s parity sentence but deny that any actual case meets it. Otto's inscriptions have only derived content, Otto's retrieval uses vision and motor control that Inga's does not, and coupling a process to its surroundings does not extend it. So cognition is brain-bound as a contingent fact, and human-plus-tool systems are too motley for a science. | Read |
| [NOTE-369](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-369.md) | Chalmers — Foreword to Supersizing the Mind | Ten years after [LIT-097](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-097.md), its co-author says the iPhone has made the thesis vivid, that the only principled objection is the perception-action boundary, and that the right reply is to let belief-ascription follow explanatory purpose, so that Otto's belief is extended for some explanations and not others. Consciousness probably stays internal, because no twin case for it can be built. The thesis needs only a weak parity-style functionalism. | Read |
| [NOTE-370](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-370.md) | Shanahan, McDonell & Reynolds — Role play with large language models (read for the self) | Read for the self. The simulator has no beliefs, goals or agency, "not even simulated versions"; simulacra only role-play characters that have them, so when an agent says "I" there is "no-one at home". The paper names, and does not answer, the question of which self a dialogue agent would act to preserve: hardware, process or instance. The denial of a self follows from the framing; no argument rules out a conscious actor behind the roles. | Read |
| [NOTE-373](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-373.md) | Survival and Identity | What matters in survival is the R-relation (mental continuity and connectedness among person-stages), and it is also identity, because persons are maximal R-interrelated aggregates of stages and so the relation of being stages of one person is the R-relation. Fission and fusion become persons sharing stages, counted by tensed identity; the long-lived Methuselah is a continuum of overlapping persons; degrees come from supervaluation over cut-offs. Against Perry's lifetimes, two persons, not three, take part in a fission. | Read |
| [NOTE-376](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-376.md) | Shanahan — Palatable Conceptions of Disembodied Being | An avowedly "poetic" attempt to fit consciousness and selfhood to a disembodied 2024 chat agent. Its time would be discrete and discontinuous. Its "I" can be the model or a conversation-bound self that flickers into being each turn; we may slip between them. Such selves can be copied, edited and merged, and spread over branching simulacra. No candidate site survives scrutiny, which is read as Buddhist emptiness and applied back to human selves. Examples are invented usages, not data. | Read |
| [NOTE-380](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-380.md) | Adams & Aizawa — Defending the Bounds of Cognition | A reply to a manuscript of Clark's "Memento's Revenge". It names the coupling-constitution fallacy, coupled is not part of, and restates the 2001 marks of the cognitive. Against Clark's Euler-circle case it separates how a diagram gets its meaning from how a mental image of it does. Against a "brain-tool science" it argues that tools are an open-ended motley. The fallacy is shown by one analogy, and the processing differences are asserted, not measured. | Read |
| [NOTE-382](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-382.md) | Shanahan — Simulacra as Conscious Exotica | A Wittgensteinian treatment: consciousness talk is anchored in what is public, so an exotic entity is a candidate only if we could engineer an encounter with it in a shared world. Disembodied chat agents are not candidates; virtually embodied ones could be. On the self: no "self worth preserving" without body, history and autobiographical memory, and no "person behind the mask" for a role player, whose identity is a shifting distribution of roles. Argued by method and scenario; nothing is measured. | Read |
| [NOTE-388](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-388.md) | Social ontology: Some basic principles | Searle restates the 1995 theory in twenty pages. Social facts are facts involving collective intentionality. Institutional facts are the subclass in which collective acceptance imposes a status function, "X counts as Y in C", carrying deontic powers that give desire-independent reasons for action. Language is constitutive, since such facts exist only as represented. He revises the book in two places: status indicators matter in their own right, and some Y terms are free-standing, with no X, as with corporations and money without currency. "We accept (S has power (S does A))", a formula from later in the book, is now ranked as the more general form. Collective intentionality is assumed, not argued for. | Read |
| [NOTE-393](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-393.md) | Epstein — Social Ontology (SEP) | A survey organised by its author's own distinction: what grounds a social fact versus what anchors the category it falls under. It reports that ontological individualism is widely assumed and now contested; that grounding has displaced supervenience; that convention, collective acceptance, patterns, practices and language are rival theories of anchoring; and that whether anchoring is a distinct relation is disputed. It covers groups, group agency, institutions, race and gender, artifacts, money, law and language. Survey claims are reported, not argued; one citation (Epstein 2016) is missing from the bibliography, and Schwitzgebel 2015 is listed with critics of group phenomenal states. | Read |
| [NOTE-394](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-394.md) | Haslanger — Gender and Race: (What) Are They? | An explicitly ameliorative ("analytical") account. Gender and race are defined as hierarchical social positions: a woman is someone regularly observed or imagined to have bodily features presumed to indicate a female's reproductive role, marked by that within the dominant ideology for subordinate positions, and subordinated in part because of it. The commonality and normativity objections are met by appeal to the project's values. Stipulative, with no evidence. | Read |
| [NOTE-395](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-395.md) | Hindriks & Guala — Institutions, rules, and equilibria | Institutions are correlated equilibria of coordination games with several equilibria, represented by the players as rules. Searle's constitutive rules are derived from a regulative rule by coining a term that splits it into a base rule and a status rule; the term is conservative and eliminable, so constitutive rules add a name and cognitive economy, not a new kind of fact. The derivation is shown for one toy institution and asserted in general. The reply adds that normativity needs no constitutive rules, because a right is a bundle of other people's regulative obligations. | Read |
| [NOTE-430](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-430.md) | Relational Frame Theory: Some Implications for Understanding and Treating Human Psychopathology | RFT stated for clinicians. Human relating is bidirectional and arbitrarily applicable, a generalized operant under contextual control, with mutual and combinatorial entailment and transformation of function. | [NOTE-490](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-490.md) | Block — The Mind as the Software of the Brain | An introductory chapter that says what the computer model of the mind claims and defends it. Intelligence is explained by functional decomposition into primitive processors; meaning-respecting processing by an isomorphism between syntactic and semantic functions that must hold counterfactually; intentionality by a language of thought whose symbols get meaning from functional role. The Turing test, Stich's syntactic theory and Searle's Chinese room are criticised. Block grants the model for intelligence and intentionality and doubts it for phenomenal consciousness. | Read |
| [NOTE-492](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-492.md) | Block — Functional Role and Truth Conditions | A use (functional role) theory of meaning must say why 'aluminum conducts electricity' has different truth conditions on Earth and Twin Earth. Internal inferential roles cannot, and appeals to referential uses beg the question. A public-use theory can only do it with long-arm roles that import the devices of a theory of reference, and the result is equivalent to a two-factor theory whose internal part is narrow meaning. Burge's arthritis cases further require role in a language, structured by deference, alongside individual roles. | Read |
| [NOTE-503](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-503.md) | Block — Advertisement for a Semantics for Psychology | Block advertises two-factor conceptual role semantics as the only approach that could meet eight desiderata for a semantics serving cognitive science. Narrow meaning is an expression's short-armed conceptual role, its abstracted causal role in reasoning and deliberation; a separate factor relates it to referents. Conceptual role explains behaviour shared across Twin Earth, learning without definitions, relativity of meaning to representational system, and the inheritance of public meaning from the language of thought. Harman's long-arm roles reduce to the same two factors, and Gricean and indicator semantics either are not naturalistic or fail. | Read |
